Beyond the visible lesion: mycotoxin attenuation and spatial heterogeneity in maize cobs
nodes.venue: Mycotoxin Research
nodes.abstract: Abstract Visible mould is widely used as a practical sorting cue in maize, but it remains unclear whether the visible lesion marks the boundary of mycotoxin contamination within an intact cob. This study examined mycotoxin attenuation, spatial heterogeneity, and co-occurrence in visibly mouldy white maize cobs, using measured distances from the visible mould margin. Cobs with visible mould ( n = 35) were sampled for the study. For each cob, the visible mould margin was coded as 0 mm, and adjacent sections were collected at the 50% and 75% points along the measured distance from the lesion boundary to the distal cob tip, resulting in 98 cob-section observations. Mycotoxins, FUMs (FB1, FB2, FB3), deoxynivalenol (DON), zearalenone (ZEA), nivalenol (NIV) and AF (AFB1) were quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Samples with no detectable levels of mycotoxins were replaced with zero, and total FUMs were calculated (FB1 + FB2 + FB3). The visible mould margin accounted for the largest share of the measured toxin burden, accounting for 84.4% of total FUM, 89.4% of DON, 77.8% of ZEA, and 92.2% of NIV. Adjacent sections retained measurable residual mycotoxins, including 15.6% of total FUM, 10.6% of DON, 22.2% of ZEA, and 7.8% of NIV. In full-distance models, DON, ZEA, and NIV declined significantly with distance, whereas total FUM did not show significant monotonic attenuation. The AFB1 was detected in only three cob sections; these detections co-occurred with Fusarium -associated toxins. Co-occurrence analysis showed that adjacent sections frequently remained positive for multiple Fusarium -associated toxin groups, with the FUM + DON + ZEA profile persisting across measured-distance bands. These findings show that visible mould is a useful warning signal but not a reliable toxicological boundary. The results support cob-level rejection or segregation of visibly mouldy cobs before shelling, rather than lesion-level trimming, as a more defensible food-safety control measure.

nodes.name: Breaking GUI Agent Actions: Realistic Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal LLMs
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has enabled GUI agents that interpret interface screenshots and execute natural-language instructions. However, their increasing role in human–computer interaction raises security concerns. Existing work shows that MLLMs are highly sensitive to interface perturbations, yet most attacks assume unrealistic capabilities such as direct access to model-ready inputs. In real deployments, attackers cannot control the screenshot pipeline or the non-differentiable preprocessing operations preceding inference, rendering many prior attacks ineffective. We introduce Realistic Adversarial Attack (RAA) framework that models the complete screenshot-to-prediction pipeline. To address gradient blockage from non-differentiable preprocessing (e.g., resizing and quantization), we develop a dual-branch differentiable preprocessing module that restores gradient flow while remaining faithful to the actual inference path. To improve robustness against query phrasing changes, we further incorporate a task-level semantic variation mechanism that jointly optimizes over paraphrased task variants. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct and GUI-Owl-7B show that RAA consistently outperforms prior attacks, improving attack success rates by an average of 30% under localized perturbations and a 10.7% under global perturbations, while maintaining strong effectiveness against standard defenses such as resizing, compression, and noise. Ablation studies highlight the roles of perturbation region and semantic diversity. Our framework establishes a practical threat model for GUI agents and offers a foundation for future robustness and security research.

nodes.name: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
ME-YOLO: Aircraft Corrosion Defect Detection Model Based on Multi-Directional Edge Perception and Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: Detecting surface defects on aircraft is critical to safety in the aerospace field. The current detection methods suffer from low efficiency, high false positive rate and poor adaptability to complex environment. Although the existing target detection algorithms have achieved notable performance in this field, at present, many models in this field still face considerable challenges. For example, due to the constraints of hardware platforms, machines that can be deployed on edge devices such as UAVs and robots need lightweight and easy-to-deploy models, but lightweight designs often a certain degree of accuracy degradation. At the same time, most of the surface defects of the aircraft are small targets, which impose higher demands on the model. In order to solve these limitations, this paper proposes an improved YOLO model ME-YOLO (multi directional edge fusion YOLO) based on edge enhancement and multi-scale fusion. Firstly, the EdgePyramid module is designed, which uses the rich edge responses extracted by the Multi Orientation Attention Sobel (MOAS) module and through the three-layer cascade pool structure to construct the three-scale edge features aligned with the backbone network. Then, the EdgeEnhance module is introduced to adaptively fuse the conventional convolution features and edge features at the corresponding resolution, effectively enhancing the sensitivity of the model to the corrosion boundary. Experimental results show that, compared with the baseline YOLOv11, ME-YOLO improves mAP@0.5 by 2.7% and simultaneously increases Recall by 2.3%, which helps reduce missed detections of corrosion targets. Although the introduction of multi-directional edge priors brings a slight increase in parameters (+3.66M) and a minor decrease in inference speed (--8.6%), the model still maintains a real-time detection capability of 97.54 FPS, meeting the deployment requirements for edge devices such as UAVs. This strategy of trading a modest computational overhead for improved detection rates in safety-critical tasks offers a potentially practical and robust alternative for intelligent operation and maintenance of aviation equipment.

nodes.name: Geosynchronous Orbit Satellite Maneuver Detection Method Based on Dual-Model Parallel GLRT
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: Ground-based radar can obtain high-precision radial velocity measurements through coherent integration Doppler processing, providing an important data source for geostationary orbit (GEO) satellite maneuver detection. An orbital maneuver causes a persistent mean shift in radial velocity residuals, whereas attitude motion or tumbling due to malfunction induces velocity scintillation, which manifests as a sudden variance amplification. Since both anomalies cause velocity residuals to deviate significantly from normal levels, a single detection model can easily misclassify one as the other. To address this problem, a maneuver detection method is proposed that combines precise orbit determination with a dual-model parallel Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT). A high-accuracy initial state is first obtained through the Gibbs method and weighted least squares. Two detection models are then constructed based on distinct residual characteristics: mean shift for maneuver detection and variance amplification for scintillation detection. An ε-contaminated Gaussian mixture GLRT detector is introduced to suppress the influence of outliers. Combined with Monte Carlo threshold calibration and a maneuver-priority competitive decision strategy, the method effectively distinguishes between the two anomaly types. Simulation results demonstrate that under strict false alarm constraints, the detection probability for both maneuvers and velocity scintillation exceeds 0.9, effectively eliminating mutual misclassification. The method achieves stable detection of weak maneuvers lasting tens of seconds with radial velocity increments of approximately 0.03 m/s, demonstrating strong engineering application potential.

nodes.name: Configuration Design and Implementation of the SuperView Neo 2 Satellite System
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: With the rapid advancement of spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology, distributed Interferometric SAR (InSAR) has emerged as the definitive method for high-precision global topographic mapping. This study focuses on the SuperView Neo 2 (SVN2) satellite system, developed by China Siwei Surveying and Mapping Technology Co., Ltd., detailing its technical configuration design and operational implementation within the next-generation commercial remote sensing sector. Equipped with X-band high-performance phased-array SAR payloads, the SVN2 system is engineered for the high-efficiency production of global 1:25,000-scale Digital Surface Models (DSM) while providing millimeter-level surface deformation monitoring through Differential InSAR (DInSAR) capabilities. The paper emphasizes a systematic design approach that integrates four coupled elements: mission objectives, system performance, orbit design, and formation geometry. To satisfy the rigorous requirements of interferometric mapping, the system adopts a sun-synchronous, strictly repeating frozen orbit with a 200-meter radius “pipeline” control strategy. By implementing flexible formation configurations for high and low latitudes, SVN2 achieves the triple synchronization of time, space, and phase necessary for sub-meter resolution and high vertical accuracy. Using the SVN2-03/04 cluster as a primary case study, the results demonstrate that through a sequence of over 40 precise orbital maneuvers, the dual-satellite system successfully established a close-range fly-around formation within the 100-meter-level pipeline just seven days after launch. This operational success represents three major technical breakthroughs for Chinese commercial radar satellites: high-precision strictly repeating orbit maintenance, stable close-range formation flying, and fully autonomous inter-satellite cooperative control. The SVN2 constellation provides a robust, all-weather mapping guarantee for the global geographic information framework and supports diverse applications in geological hazard detection and social economic planning.

nodes.name: Pre-Event DEM-Based Deep-Seated Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using a Vision Transformer in the Kii Mountains, Japan
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: This study evaluates deep-seated landslide susceptibility using pre-event LiDAR-derived DEM data from the 2011 Kii Peninsula heavy rainfall disaster. Terrain parameters representing gravitational deformation were calculated and used as inputs to compare a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Vision Transformer (ViT). Validation results show that ViT achieved higher classification accuracy (0.867) than CNN (0.837), with recall for the landslide class exceeding 95%. ViT effectively captured broader geomorphological context, whereas CNN emphasized local terrain features. Both models showed difficulty in distinguishing DSGSD, reflecting its intermediate geomorphic characteristics. Tests in unseen areas indicate the potential to identify terrain prone to future failure using pre-event topography alone.

Multimodal Physiotherapy in Right Frozen Shoulder: A Case Report
nodes.venue: JURNAL KEPERAWATAN DAN FISIOTERAPI (JKF)
nodes.abstract: Background: Frozen shoulder, or adhesive capsulitis, is a condition characterized by pain and limited range of motion in the shoulder joint that can interfere with daily functional activities. Multimodal physical therapy is necessary to manage pain, improve mobility, and restore shoulder function. Objective: To determine the effectiveness of physical therapy management using Infrared (IR), Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS), and scapular mobilization in a patient with stiffness of the right shoulder due to frozen shoulder. Methods: This study is a case report of a 61-year-old male patient who had complained of pain and limited movement in his right shoulder for two weeks prior to examination. Physical therapy interventions were administered twice weekly over four sessions, including 15 minutes of mild-intensity IR, 10 minutes of conventional TENS at 80–100 Hz, and scapular mobilization exercises consisting of shoulder shrug exercises performed 8–10 repetitions in 2–3 sets. Evaluation was conducted using range of motion (ROM) measurements, the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), and Manual Muscle Testing (MMT). Results: There was an improvement in range of motion, particularly in shoulder flexion from 50° to 80°, as well as improvements in abduction and rotation, although these were not significant. Pain decreased from a score of 7/10 to 5/10 after four therapy sessions. However, muscle strength did not show a significant improvement.

nodes.name: Modeling corporate financial distress using explainable machine learning: evidence from macro-financial panel data
nodes.venue: Journal of Modelling in Management
nodes.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether firm-level market indicators and lagged macroeconomic information can be integrated within an explainable predictive framework for corporate financial distress, with particular attention to temporal dynamics, model performance and interpretability. Design/methodology/approach This study uses an unbalanced panel of 15,664 firm-month observations from 99 large-cap US listed equity series covering July 2012–September 2025. Regularized logistic regression, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting and XGBoost are evaluated using chronological training, validation and held-out testing. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) provide model interpretability, while alternative macroeconomic lag structures, calibration diagnostics and robustness checks assess the stability of the predictive evidence. Findings Regularized logistic regression records the strongest full-test point estimates (AUC = 0.7886; average precision = 0.3085), while XGBoost is the strongest nonlinear benchmark (AUC = 0.7314; average precision = 0.2049). However, model rankings vary across evaluation periods. The combined one-, three- and six-month lag specification performs best, indicating that predictive macroeconomic information is distributed across multiple horizons. SHAP identifies 63-day firm-level volatility as the leading XGBoost feature and reveals conditional relationships between macroeconomic conditions and firm-specific vulnerability. Research limitations/implications The large-cap US sample, market-based distress definition and mixed-frequency design limit broader generalization. Practical implications The framework can support risk ranking, early-warning screening and interpretable financial-risk monitoring for investors, financial institutions and regulators. Originality/value This study integrates temporal macroeconomic information, comparative model evaluation and explainable AI, demonstrating that greater model complexity does not necessarily improve out-of-sample distress prediction.

nodes.name: Machine Learning Weather Prediction: Models, Verification and Limits
nodes.venue: International Journal of Information Technology Research Studies (IJITRS)
nodes.abstract: Between 2022 and 2025 a series of neural networks trained on four decades of reanalysis data began to match, and on many headline scores to beat, the best physics-based global weather forecasts, at a small fraction of the running cost. This review describes that change for an information technology readership and reports no new experiment. We begin with the numerical baseline and the ERA5 reanalysis on which nearly all of the models are trained. We then follow the deterministic models built on convolutions, neural operators, transformers and graph networks, the probabilistic and hybrid systems that came after them, and precipitation nowcasting from radar and satellite as a neighbouring problem. Benchmarks and published scores are then set beside the critical studies, which found forecasts that blur as lead time grows, weak physical balance at small scales, missing error growth from tiny perturbations, underestimated wind peaks in individual storms and poorer skill on record-breaking extremes. The same body of work also found realistic dynamical behaviour, and we report both sides. Compute cost, explainability and the dependence on numerical analyses for training and initial states close the review.

Integrating Satellite Surface Reflectance and Field Measurements to Predict Moisture Content Profiles in Bare-Soil Conditions
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: Landslides triggered by rainfall infiltration pose significant geotechnical hazards, yet predictive modeling remains limited by the lack of scalable, high-resolution soil moisture data. This study develops a machine learning-based Hydro/Spectral (H/S) model to predict volumetric water content (VWC) at multiple soil depths using Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery and in-situ soil temperature measurements from ten Kentucky Mesonet stations. Over 500 cloud-free images were processed within 160 m × 160 m bare-soil buffers, an area of interest significantly finer than the kilometer-scale resolutions typical of most satellite-based soil moisture predictions. For each image, statistical descriptors such as skewness, variance, and covariance eigenvalues were extracted from reflectance data in visible, near infrared, and shortwave infrared bands. These features were paired with daily in-situ measurements to train and validate multiple regression models. Random Forest outperformed other models, achieving the highest R² and lowest RMSE across all depths. Soil temperature and spectral indices such as the Normalized Difference Soil Index (NDSI) were identified as key predictors. Results demonstrate that reflectance and climate data can predict shallow soil moisture with moderate accuracy at fine spatial scales. This approach supports the development of scalable, non-invasive tools for monitoring unsaturated soil conditions and improving slope stability assessments under changing climate conditions.

nodes.name: Evaluating the Propagation of Geological Uncertainty from Ground Model to Geotechnical Analysis
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: Engineering geological ground models integrate information from field investigations, laboratory tests, and geological interpretation. However, due to the sparsity and imperfection of these input data and the natural variability of geomaterials, ground models inherently contain uncertainty. One important aspect is addressed as geological uncertainty, which relates to unknown stratigraphic boundaries and the spatial arrangement of geotechnical units. While established metrics for geological uncertainty quantification, e.g., information entropy, can highlight regions with ambiguous geological classifications, they provide limited insight into how this uncertainty may affect the geotechnical system performance downstream. To address the propagation of geological uncertainty in complex boundary value problems, this study applies a Monte Carlo simulation framework that couples stochastic ground modeling with geomechanical finite element analyses. The approach is hierarchical: first, a probabilistic ground model is defined based on the geological scenario; then, an ensemble of observation-consistent realizations is generated; finally, each realization serves as input to a deterministic geomechanical analysis using standard commercial finite element codes. The resulting ensemble statistics from the geotechnical analyses provide insight into how geological uncertainty propagates to geomechanical response variability, supporting transparent uncertainty communication, risk assessment and decision-making.

nodes.name: CPT-Based Prediction of Total Foundation Settlement in Sensitive and Compressible Deltaic Soils: Case Reviews from the Niger Delta, Nigeria
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: Settlement prediction is a major challenge for foundation design in the Niger Delta because deltaic deposits commonly comprise interbedded soft clay, silty clay, peat, sand and organic sediments with pronounced spatial variability and high compressibility. Conventional settlement assessment based exclusively on boreholes and oedometer tests may be affected by sampling disturbance, limited vertical resolution and scale effects. This study evaluates the use of cone penetration testing (CPT) for estimating immediate and consolidation settlement, using three case reviews from the Niger Delta. CPT cone resistance, sleeve friction and, where available, pore-pressure information were interpreted to establish soil stratigraphy and derive compressibility and deformation parameters. Immediate settlement was estimated using CPT-derived deformation moduli, while primary consolidation settlement was evaluated using constrained-modulus and empirical CPT correlations, including the approaches of de Beer and Martens, Sanglerat, Kulhawy and Mayne, and Lunne et al. The predicted settlements were compared with settlements calculated from borehole and oedometer data. The case studies demonstrate that CPT provides a high-resolution representation of subsurface variability and generally produces settlement estimates comparable with conventional analyses. In the Warri–Sombreiro Deltaic Plain, CPT-predicted total settlements ranged from 32.8 to 76 mm, compared with 29.7–58.1 mm from conventional analyses at the centres of the investigated foundations. In the Coastal Plain Sands, CPT predictions were generally of the same order as borehole-based estimates, although individual locations showed appreciable differences. The results indicate that CPT is a reliable and efficient settlement-screening and design-support tool when correlations are appropriately calibrated and supplemented by targeted borehole and laboratory investigations. CPTu dissipation testing provides an additional opportunity for estimating consolidation rate. The study proposes an integrated CPT–borehole–laboratory framework for foundation investigations in heterogeneous Niger Delta sediments.

nodes.name: Advancing Remote Sensing for Semantic Landslide Hazard Mapping and Monitoring
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: Landslide hazard assessment and monitoring have traditionally relied on visual interpretation and heuristic classification methods, often limiting the spatial and temporal resolution of actionable insights. Recent advances in remote sensing technologies and machine learning offer new opportunities to automate and enhance the semantic understanding of landslide processes across diverse terrains. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates very high-resolution remote sensing data with semantic segmentation and classification algorithms to improve the accuracy, consistency, and interpretability of landslide hazard. Using a multi-sensor fusion approach, the framework applies deep learning-based semantic classification to differentiate landslide-prone areas from stable terrain and to identify geomorphic features, including scarp zones, depositional zones, and tension cracks. Time-series analysis enables continuous monitoring and detection of precursory signals, supporting dynamic hazard assessment and monitoring. The method is validated in complex coastal and mountainous environments with diverse lithologies and land cover, demonstrating robust performance in both detecting active landslides and mapping specific zones. This research highlights the potential of semantic remote sensing approaches for scalable, data-driven landslide hazard mapping and monitoring. The results support more informed decision-making for early warning systems, infrastructure planning, and disaster risk reduction in landslide-prone regions.

nodes.name: Adaptive design of Emergency spillway repairs at the Akosombo Dam: Integrating CFD, Scour Model and FEM under time constraints
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: The Akosombo Dam Spillway No. 2 repair project addressed an urgent engineering challenge following severe erosion of the downstream rock foundation during a major spillage in October 2023. The 2023 spilling event at Akosombo Dam Spillway No. 2 resulted in severe scour of the downstream rock foundation, creating an urgent need for both immediate stabilisation and a long-term protection strategy. This paper presents the multidisciplinary adaptive design approach used to develop and construct a permanent remedial measure under extreme time, material, and logistical constraints. A parallel workflow combining site investigations, geological mapping, hydraulic assessments, structural design, and geotechnical analyses was adopted to support rapid decision-making. For the permanent solution, an integrated modelling framework was developed, combining Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), three-dimensional scour modelling, and Finite Element Method (FEM) analyses. CFD simulations were used to evaluate jet trajectories, impact pressures, and hydraulic loading conditions, while calibrated scour models assessed the evolution of erosion under different spilling scenarios. These outputs were incorporated into a PLAXIS 2D geotechnical model to evaluate global stability, structural performance, and the effects of progressive scour on the remedial works. The final design consists of an enhanced reinforced concrete protection slab integrated with a palisade retaining wall system and scour protection measures founded on the underlying rock mass. Model calibration against the 2023 event increased confidence in hydraulic loading assumptions and rock mass behaviour, while sensitivity analyses confirmed stability under conservative scour conditions. The project demonstrates how the combination of CFD, scour prediction, and geotechnical FEM modelling can be effectively integrated within an adaptive design framework to deliver resilient dam infrastructure solutions under conditions of geological uncertainty, operational constraints, and increasing hydrological extremes.

nodes.name: 3D Geological Subsurface Model as a Supporting Engineering Tool for the Einstein Telescope Study Area in Sardinia (Italy)
nodes.venue: IAEG 2026: Engineering Geology in a Rapidly Changing World - XV IAEG World Congress
nodes.abstract: The Einstein Telescope (ET) research infrastructure is envisioned as Europe’s first next-generation underground observatory for gravitational-wave detection. Its engineering design requires a multidisciplinary and multi-criteria approach capable of identifying and addressing geological, geotechnical, environmental, and landscape-related challenges. Particular attention must be paid to site conditions and physical characteristics that could influence the performance of the scientific instruments. To address these complexities, a collaborative effort involving the scientific and engineering communities led to the development of an advanced, multi-scale 3D digital model of the Sardinia site, identified as a potential location for the ET infrastructure. The model integrates surface and subsurface information at both regional and local scales, consolidating all available geological, geophysical, and geotechnical datasets into a coherent reconstruction of the main subsurface features, including lithological units, faults, and fracture networks. It incorporates data derived from surface investigations and calibration boreholes, including geological and petrophysical information, laboratory analyses of undisturbed samples, fracture characterization, and geophysical surveys conducted by the ET scientific community. This integrated framework significantly strengthens the correlation between surface observations and subsurface structures. The resulting model enables the extraction of three-dimensional geological prognoses, transforming it from a visualization platform into a predictive engineering tool. This advanced modelling approach supports the mitigation of geotechnical risks, the optimization of construction strategies, and the implementation of scenario-based design analyses. The model is being made available to the ET scientific community and is already supporting several applications, including physics-based investigations of Newtonian noise.

nodes.name: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
nodes.venue: Science Advances
nodes.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

nodes.name: LARVA-Net: A Bio-Inspired Recursive Attention Model for IoT-Based Microclimate Prediction in Black Soldier Fly Insectariums
nodes.venue: JURNAL TEKNIK INFORMATIKA
nodes.abstract: Microclimate prediction is critical for optimizing larval growth and productivity in Black Soldier Fly (BSF) insectariums, where temperature and humidity exhibit nonlinear and time-varying dynamics. Conventional models such as Vector Autoregression (VAR) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) often struggle to balance accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability in IoT-based environments. This study proposes LARVA-Net, a bio-inspired recursive attention framework for multivariate microclimate prediction in BSF insectariums. LARVA-Net integrates a VAR-based linear baseline with selective recursive attention and adaptive fuzzy-state learning. The bio-inspired aspect represents a computational abstraction of adaptive and energy-efficient information processing observed in larval behavior, rather than a biological simulation. By selectively updating internal states based on contextual relevance, the model suppresses error accumulation while maintaining interpretability and stable learning. The proposed method is evaluated using real-world IoT microclimate data collected from a semi-controlled BSF insectarium. Experimental results show that LARVA-Net outperforms VAR, ANFIS, and VARFIS, achieving an RMSE of 0.2440, MAE of 0.1466, MAPE of 0.4566%, and R² of 0.9911. These results demonstrate strong predictive performance and robustness under time-aware evaluation, indicating the suitability of LARVA-Net for real-time IoT-based microclimate monitoring in resource-constrained environments.

nodes.name: An electric-potential-augmented benchmark dataset for electrical capacitance tomography: electric-potential supervision for future physics-guided learning
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract While deep learning has significantly advanced image reconstruction of electrical capacitance tomography (ECT), most public datasets retain only capacitance vectors and permittivity distributions and do not expose the excitation-wise electric potential field, a physical intermediate in the forward mapping. To address this, we present an electric-potential-augmented ECT benchmark dataset generated via a COMSOL–MATLAB pipeline for a fixed eight-electrode sensor. The dataset comprises 20 000 randomized samples across four typical flow-pattern families. Alongside conventional capacitance vectors and permittivity images, each sample preserves eight spatially registered full-field potential maps. Governing equations and field-perturbation visualizations characterize the relation between potential and dielectric structure. As an initial use of this physical information, we introduce potential-field intermediate supervision to guide representation learning in simple forward and inverse models. Under sample-disjoint independent and identically distributed (IID) and fully held-out two-bar out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation, potential supervision reduces forward capacitance-prediction mean squared error (MSE) by 56.8% and 74.6%, respectively, relative to a structure- and capacity-aligned control. In an exploratory forward experiment, a low-weight partial differential equation residual yields 5.3%–8.3% lower mean potential-prediction MSE. For inverse reconstruction, the simple model reduces mean MSE by 14.3% and 3.0% on IID and OOD data, respectively, relative to the same control. The more modest inverse gains are consistent with the difficulty of recovering dense potential maps from limited capacitance measurements. These results provide initial controlled evidence for the value of potential-field supervision. The dataset and reference experiments together offer a foundation and methodological insights for developing more advanced field-supervised, physics-informed, and data-consistent ECT methods.

nodes.name: CoBiDiff: anatomy-aware bidirectional diffusion for left atrium cross-modal augmentation
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate delineation of the left atrium (LA) from cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) and computed tomography (CT) images plays an important role in atrial fibrillation assessment and treatment planning. However, the limited availability of expert-annotated cardiac datasets restricts the robustness and generalizability of deep learning–based segmentation models, particularly in cross-modal scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose CoBiDiff, a collaborative bidirectional diffusion framework that explicitly incorporates anatomical constraints into unpaired cross-modal cardiac image augmentation. The framework is developed using unpaired CT and MR volumes from the MICCAI 2017 multi-modality whole heart segmentation (MM-WHS) challenge dataset, focusing specifically on the LA region. A shared diffusion backbone is employed to jointly model both imaging modalities, while signed distance functions (SDFs) are incorporated as structural representations to provide anatomical guidance during generation. To reduce the influence of artificial CT field-of-view boundaries, boundary regions are suppressed through noise replacement and gradient smoothing strategies. In addition, a soft spatial extent loss is introduced to maintain anatomically plausible foreground spatial extents during synthesis. An SDF dropout strategy is further introduced during training to strengthen image-conditioned anatomical inference and improve anatomical coherence. Experimental results indicate that the proposed framework generates LA images with improved structural consistency across modalities. The proposed method achieved Dice coefficients of 86.53% and 95.04%, and average symmetric surface distances of 1.511 mm and 0.623 mm for CT-to-MR and MR-to-CT augmentation, respectively, on the MM-WHS 2017 dataset. CoBiDiff provides a practical framework for expanding limited cardiac imaging datasets without requiring paired cross-modal images. By combining diffusion-based synthesis with anatomy-aware constraints, CoBiDiff improves the downstream utility of generated samples for cardiac segmentation. The full implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/PencilSC/CoBiDiff to support reproducible and open research.

nodes.name: Fostering Cultural Self‑Awareness through Culturally Responsive Teaching: A Case Study of EFL Pedagogy in Chinese Higher Education
nodes.venue: Journal of Qualitative Research in Education
nodes.abstract: In many Chinese university English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms, culture is still presented as a collection of factual information regarding festivals, foods, and other visible symbols. Students may recognize these items without being able to explain what they mean or to discuss Chinese cultural experience critically in English. This study develops and examines a localized Culturally Responsive Teaching (CRT) sequence designed to foster cultural self-awareness and cultural narrative competence through three stages: critically unpacking cultural representations, comparing local and foreign cultural practices, and producing multimodal narratives. A single-group pre-post mixed-methods case study was conducted with 29 first-year engineering students at a local university over a 16-week semester. Evidence came from Likert questionnaires, language tests, classroom worksheets and mind maps, oral presentations, and English vlogs assessed with a three-dimensional rubric for cultural self-awareness, linguistic performance, and multimodal production. The results show the largest gains in cultural self-awareness and multimodal storytelling, with more modest progress in linguistic accuracy. Classroom records suggest that comparative inquiry and hometown-based vlog work helped students move beyond naming cultural objects toward explaining their social and personal significance. These findings provide preliminary, triangulated evidence associated with the localized CRT sequence and illustrate how CRT can be operationalized through comparative inquiry and multimodal cultural narrative production in Chinese university EFL instruction. The study also offers an empirically grounded pedagogical model and a basis for further comparative research on culturally responsive EFL pedagogy.
